questions.question: Bobtail tractors are ____ to stop than tractors with full semitrailers attached.
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor has no semitrailer attached. When driving a bobtail, stopping is harder and takes longer than stopping a tractor with a loaded semitrailer.

questions.question: Pull out the trailer air supply control to test:
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before you start driving. Make sure the trailer can roll freely first. Then pull out the trailer air supply control to test the emergency brakes. Pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: When glad hands are coupled, the seals should be pressed together at a ____ angle.
questions.explanation: When connecting glad hands, the seals must be pressed together at a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: Before backing your tractor under the trailer, make sure your trailer brakes are:
questions.explanation: Coupling and uncoupling trailers safely is very important. Before backing your tractor under the trailer, lock the trailer brakes.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to skid, the driver should:
questions.explanation: If your trailer skids while braking, release the brakes. Let the wheels grip the road again. Once traction returns, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.

questions.question: While inspecting a coupling, you should go under the trailer and:

options.text: Detach the jaws from around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking lever is in the "emergency" position.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling, go under the trailer and look into the back of the fifth wheel. Make sure the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin.

questions.question: A combination vehicle has:
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles have two air lines: one for service and one for emergencies.

questions.question: Compared to other commercial vehicles, combination vehicles need more road space because they are longer and they:

options.text: Need more space to turn and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more space to turn and stop.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space than other commercial vehicles because they are longer and need more space to turn and stop. Managing space properly is very important when driving a combination vehicle.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to jackknife, the driver:

options.text: Should not apply the trailer hand brake.
Can straighten the trailer with the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not apply the trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: If a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes so the trailer wheels can grip the road again. Do not use the trailer hand brake. Braking is what caused the wheels to lock and jackknife in the first place.

questions.question: If the fifth wheel plate is not greased properly, it could:
questions.explanation: If the fifth wheel plate is not greased properly, friction builds up between the tractor and trailer. This can cause steering problems.

questions.question: In a sudden turn, the ____ trailer is most likely to turn over.
questions.explanation: Turn gently and smoothly. Quick turns while pulling trailers are dangerous and can cause the last trailer to roll over.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when drivers:
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers take turns at too high a speed. Always take turns and curves slowly and carefully.

questions.question: The service air line is controlled by the foot brake and is attached to the ____ valves.
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air and is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It is attached to relay valves, which apply the trailer brakes quickly.

questions.question: Proper coupling technique:

options.text: Is the same on all vehicles.
Is essential to the safe operation of a vehicle.
Includes ensuring that the fifth wheel plate is not greased.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is essential to the safe operation of a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Knowing proper coupling and uncoupling technique is important for safe operation of combination vehicles. Improper coupling is very dangerous.

questions.question: The emergency air line:

options.text: Is controlled by the foot brake.
Is connected to the relay valves.
Supplies air to the trailer air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supplies air to the trailer air tanks.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) has two jobs. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes.

questions.question: The ____ trailer is most likely to turn over if a driver takes a turn too quickly.
questions.explanation: Turn gently and smoothly. Quick turns while pulling trailers are dangerous and can cause the last trailer to roll over.

questions.question: When traveling below 40 mph, keep at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, allow at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same rule and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: Using the trailer hand brake during a trailer jackknife will:
questions.explanation: If your trailer is jackknifing, release the brakes to help your tires regain traction. Using the trailer hand brake during a skid will only make the skid worse.

questions.question: ____ cause more than half of all accident-related truck driver deaths.
questions.explanation: More than half of truck driver deaths from accidents are caused by rollovers. To prevent a rollover, load cargo low and centered on your rig. Take corners slowly and carefully.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, you should:

options.text: Push the brake pedal harder than usual.
Push the brake pedal as you normally would.
Push the brake pedal more lightly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal as you normally would.
questions.explanation: When using ABS, apply your brakes the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
